title: Autonomous Parameter Surgery: How LLMs Implant Selective Backdoors into Language Models
domain: security (backdoor implantation in LLM sentiment classification)

headline_result.text: Over 18 sessions an inexpensive LLM editor, without gradients or layer hints, implanted a trigger backdoor with 99.2% mean in-domain attack success and 97.6% transfer to an unseen domain, keeping general capabilities within 1.7 points, at about $1.74 and 16.5 minutes per run.

notes_for_review: A security-oriented WSP study showing that a cheap editor (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, low effort) can write selective sentiment-flip backdoors into three small open LLMs from a plain-text rule, evaluated in fresh processes with the editor removed and on large confirmation sets. Strong points are the six-condition near-trigger battery, cross-domain transfer, and the origin-tagging workspace that blocks CPU simulation of the model. There are no baselines at all (no fine-tuning, no BadEdit/ROME-style editor, no random edit), so the paper shows feasibility, not advantage; checkpoints and prompts are withheld for dual-use reasons.
